subject: AWS Marketplace private offer: pricing, term length, buyer approvals
body:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Smith <michael.smith@amazon.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace private offer for Acme Analytics — pricing & approvals

Hi Michael,

Following up on our call this morning — Acme Analytics (contact: Alex Johnson) is ready to move forward with an AWS Marketplace private offer. They asked for clarity on acceptable term lengths, buyer approval flow, and how discounts and committed capacity should be reflected on the private offer.

I attached our current draft of terms and the Acme pricing sheet (pricing-sheet-Acme-20260311.xlsx). High-level asks from Acme:
- 12-month commitment preferred, but open to 1- or 3-year options
- Ability for procurement to approve via the AWS console (they want to see step-by-step)
- PO issuance in parallel to private offer approval

Can you confirm the typical approval timeline on the AWS side, whether AWS accepts DocuSign for signature routing, and whether there are any constraints on showing volume discounts in the private offer listing? Also: is there a recommended default term you see close deals faster (1 vs 12 vs 36 months)?

Thanks — I cc'd Dev and Jonas to loop in pricing/SE for any tweaks.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Michael Smith <michael.smith@amazon.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aws.amazon.com
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace private offer for Acme Analytics — pricing & approvals

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. Quick answers:

1) Term length: AWS Marketplace supports flexible term lengths for private offers. The market tends to close fastest on 1-year and 3-year terms. 12-months is the sweet spot for ISVs selling SaaS subscriptions. 3-year deals can get higher discount bands but take longer to clear.

2) Buyer approvals: The buyer must accept the private offer from their AWS Marketplace console. The flow is: Seller submits private offer -> AWS validates -> Buyer receives notification -> Buyer accepts and provides billing/PO as needed. Typical validation + buyer approval timeline is 5–10 business days depending on buyer procurement cycles.

3) DocuSign: AWS will accept an attached executed agreement (DocuSign) for seller/buyer contract purposes, but the private offer acceptance itself must be done in the Marketplace console (accept button).

4) Showing discounts: You can surface committed-capacity discounts in the offer metadata and in the purchase terms. We recommend including both a line-item that maps to the SKU (so discounts apply at checkout) and a short note in the offer description. Avoid conditional language that requires separate SOWs for discount eligibility — that slows buyer acceptance.

I can help with the Seller Private Offer submission once you attach the finalized offer package (signed terms, seller ID, price list, SKU mapping). Also cc'd our procurement queue in case they need to jump in.

-Michael
Account Manager, AWS Marketplace

Marissa / team —

Thanks for looping us in. A few quick pricing/ops notes after reviewing the Acme sheet:
- If we go 12 months, suggest list price = $480k/year with a 15% private-offer discount for net $408k to match their target TCO.
- For committed capacity, we should create a dedicated SKU with a term-based price (monthly amortized) to ensure the discount applies at checkout.
- Question for legal (Lauren): can we add a 30/60-day early-termination window for buyer convenience within the first 6 months? That might help procurement greenlight faster.

Jonas — can you prepare a short SKU mapping doc and the minimal acceptance language required by AWS? I can prepare a redline to RDW_AWS_Private_Offer_Terms_v1.2.pdf and propose an opt-out clause.

Cheers,
Dev

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions on AWS private offer flow and renewal

Alex —

Thanks for the quick questions earlier. Answers inline below and next steps at the bottom.

Q: Will the private offer auto-renew?
A: Private offers do not auto-renew on the Marketplace. Renewal is a separate accept/transaction. For subscription-style consumption, we can set the offer term to 12 months and include an optional renewal notice (we recommend 60 days before expiration). If you want auto-billing without manual re-accept, we can discuss a separate arrangement tied to a payment instrument in AWS (but that typically requires additional procurement approvals).

Q: How does procurement approve it?
A: Procurement will receive a notification in the AWS Marketplace console. Steps for your team:
1) Go to AWS Marketplace -> Private Offers -> Notifications (you'll see a pending offer).
2) Click Accept -> Review pricing & terms -> Confirm purchase method (credit card or PO).
3) If PO, upload PO number and associated docs; AWS will finalize the order once the buyer uploads the PO.

Q: Do discounts apply to committed capacity?
A: Yes, if we publish a dedicated SKU for the committed-capacity product and set the private offer price accordingly. I'll attach the SKU mapping and the PO template so procurement has an example.

Next steps (proposed):
- I will upload the redlined terms and the SKU mapping to the private offer package and share the DocuSign link for signature.
- If procurement wants, Michael at AWS can do a live walkthrough of the acceptance flow.

Attached: RDW_AWS_Private_Offer_Terms_v1.2.pdf (redline coming), PO_template_AWS_private_offer.docx

Best,
Marissa Cole

Alex — attaching the PO template now (PO_template_AWS_private_offer.docx).

Regarding your 30% up-front discount question: as long as the private offer price we submit reflects that discount for the chosen billing cadence (one-time up-front vs annual amortized), the buyer experience at checkout is the same — they will see the final price and choose PO or payment instrument. The only nuance is if you require split invoices or milestone billing; that adds paperwork outside the Marketplace flow.

Expected timeline: if procurement uploads a PO and accepts the offer this week, AWS validation + acceptance typically completes within 3–7 business days. If you want to accelerate, Michael can flag the submission on the AWS side.

I'll stand by to set up a walkthrough with Michael and procurement.

Best regards,
